t: Falkenhayn planned to take the Meuse Heights so that the French would send their reserves to recapture them and suffer heavy losses; historians disagree whether attrition was his aim from the start or was put forward after the attack failed.
The battle lasted 302 days and was the longest of the First World War; Heer and Naumann calculated 377,231 French and 337,000 German casualties, while other historians give different totals.
In France Verdun came to stand for the determination of the army and the destructiveness of the war, and in 1984 Helmut Kohl and François Mitterrand stood together at the Douaumont cemetery.
dyk: Fort Douaumont, the largest fort of the Verdun region, held only a maintenance crew of about 68 technicians in February 1916, and a German party of about 100 soldiers entered it through an unmanned ditch bunker.
ev: Resources are taken from the forts of Verdun, and the railway line from Paris is closed by the German 3rd Army in mid-July
A bombardment by 808 guns opens Operation Judgement on 21 February and German infantry attack in the afternoon
German troops enter Fort Douaumont, held by a small maintenance crew
The Germans extend the offensive to the west bank to destroy the French artillery
Fort Vaux surrenders on 7 June, and the German advance of 23 June reaches Chapelle Sainte-Fine, its furthest point
Falkenhayn orders the Germans onto the defensive after the failed attack on Fort Souville
French marines and colonial infantry recapture Fort Douaumont
A French offensive under Mangin takes 11,387 prisoners and recovers the ground lost in February

f.date: 21 February to 18 December 1916 (302 days), in four phases
f.place: The hills on the right (east) bank of the Meuse north of Verdun, later also the west bank, in the Fortified Region of Verdun, north-eastern France
f.sides: Germany: the 5th Army under Crown Prince Wilhelm, within the plan of Erich von Falkenhayn, with 1,201 guns massed on the front, two thirds heavy or super-heavy. France: the Second Army and the Fortified Region of Verdun, under Philippe Pétain from late February, then Robert Nivelle, with 388 field guns and 244 heavy guns at the start of the attack
f.outcome: The Germans captured Fort Douaumont and Fort Vaux but never reached the Meuse Heights as a secure position; French counter-offensives in October and December recovered both forts and much of the ground. Casualties are put at about 714,000 in all, by Heer and Naumann and by Philpott.
